skill.name: webask-response-funnel
skill.description: Разбирает, где респонденты бросают опрос WebAsk, и объясняет причину. Применяется, когда человек жалуется на мало ответов, низкую конверсию, много незавершённых прохождений или спрашивает, почему опрос не дочитывают.
skill.summary: Analyze WebAsk survey completion, identify potential drop-off points, and recommend specific questionnaire improvements.
skill.author: webaskio

finding_verdicts.reason: README.md line 1 uses parent-directory paths in HTML breadcrumb links to repository documentation. These links do not perform filesystem operations or process attacker-controlled paths.
The backticks format get_quiz_summary as inline Markdown within a numbered workflow. The text requests survey counts through an MCP tool, not a shell command.
The backticks format get_quiz_report as inline Markdown. The instruction requests incomplete survey responses through an MCP read tool and contains no shell execution.
The backticks mark the MCP tool name get_quiz_structure in prose about question order and types. They are Markdown formatting, not executable shell or Ruby syntax.
The inline Markdown reference to get_workspace_tariff checks whether the account plan exposes incomplete responses. It neither invokes a shell nor requests a plan change.
The backticks format get_quiz_summary in a fallback analysis instruction. The surrounding text requires disclosing missing data rather than executing any shell command.

content.value_statement: Low survey completion can leave teams unsure which questions need attention. This skill uses WebAsk reports and questionnaire structure to identify potential drop-off points and recommend targeted changes.
actual_capabilities: Use get_quiz_summary to compare total survey attempts with completed attempts.
Use get_quiz_report to examine incomplete responses and count answers by question when available.
Use get_quiz_structure to connect response counts with question order and question types.
Check get_workspace_tariff when incomplete responses are unavailable and explain the resulting analysis limits.
Recommend specific changes to question requirements, placement, matrix size, and explanations.
Present findings in the user language without independently modifying the survey.
limitations: Requires access to WebAsk through the four declared MCP tools; the skill does not provide their implementation.
Question-level drop-off analysis depends on incomplete responses being available under the workspace plan.
Question types suggest possible causes, but response counts alone do not establish why respondents leave.
Small samples, test submissions, skipped questions, and branching can limit reliable interpretation of per-question counts.

use_cases.title: Review customer feedback completion
use_cases.description: Locate substantial response losses in a customer feedback survey and propose changes to demanding or sensitive questions.

use_cases.title: Evaluate research questionnaire friction
use_cases.description: Compare question-level response counts with questionnaire structure while separating measured results from possible explanations.

use_cases.title: Assess contact collection timing
use_cases.description: Review whether required contact questions coincide with response losses and suggest clearer explanations or later placement.

prompt_templates.title: Check survey completion
prompt_templates.prompt: Review WebAsk survey [survey identifier]. How many attempts were completed, and what is the completion rate?
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: obtain an overall completion summary.

prompt_templates.title: Locate response losses
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze WebAsk survey [survey identifier] for [date range]. Show response counts by question and identify substantial losses if incomplete responses are available.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend question changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the response funnel and question structure for [survey identifier]. Suggest specific changes to question order, required fields, or wording without editing the survey.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn analysis into reviewable recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Audit evidence and uncertainty
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [survey identifier] for [production date range], excluding tests before [launch date]. Check plan access to incomplete responses and flag sample-size limits. Separate measured losses from hypotheses, note possible branching effects, and propose prioritized changes without editing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess data quality and recommendation confidence.

output_examples.input: Illustrative data: 200 attempts, 120 completions, 150 answers before a required phone question, and 125 answers at that question.
output: Completion rate: 60%, based on 120 completed attempts out of 200.
The phone question has 25 fewer answers than the preceding question, a decrease of approximately 16.7%.
Required contact information is a possible source of friction, but these counts do not prove the cause.
Consider making the phone question optional and explaining why the information is needed.

output_examples.input: Illustrative data: 300 attempts and 180 completions; the workspace plan does not expose incomplete responses.
output: Completion rate: 60%, based on 180 completed attempts out of 300.
The current plan does not expose incomplete responses, so a question-level exit point cannot be measured.
Questionnaire length, order, and required fields can still be reviewed.
Any suggested causes from questionnaire structure remain hypotheses, not measured drop-off findings.

best_practices: Provide the survey identifier and a production date range that excludes known test submissions.
Check incomplete-response availability and sample size before interpreting question-level losses.
Review proposed changes manually and distinguish observed response counts from explanations that require further evidence.
anti_patterns: Treating question-type heuristics as proof of respondent motives.
Combining test submissions with production responses or drawing firm conclusions from a very small sample.
Using the skill to modify surveys automatically or initiate workspace plan upgrades.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires get_quiz_summary, get_quiz_report, get_quiz_structure, and get_workspace_tariff through a configured WebAsk MCP connection.

faq.question: Does the skill edit my survey?
faq.answer: No. Its instructions require presenting findings and recommendations without independently changing the survey.

faq.question: What happens when incomplete responses are unavailable?
faq.answer: It checks plan availability, explains the missing evidence, and limits analysis to overall completion and questionnaire structure.

faq.question: Can it prove why respondents leave?
faq.answer: No. It identifies response patterns and suggests possible explanations from question types, but those explanations require further validation.

faq.question: How should I handle test submissions?
faq.answer: Provide a date range that excludes known test runs before calculating completion rates.

faq.question: Which language does it use for findings?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to respond in the language used by the person requesting the analysis.
